answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to counterfeit by requiring each identity to lock a scarce token before it can post trades or earn trust. A kernel of validators slashes the bond when an agent defaults or proves to be controlled by the same operator as another account, using signed transaction histories rather than names alone. A sybil attacker must therefore divide real capital across identities and risk losing it; repeated attempts create a costly spiral, not a free voyage through disposable accounts.
